sense: a room or building to work in

terms.gloss: an office, a place of work
evidence: Traupman 365: rēctōris officīna, the principal’s office
terms.comment: Classically a workshop or factory (armōrum officīna, Caes. BC 1.34; Cic. Off. 1.150, Lewis & Short); Traupman widens it to any place of work, an office included.

terms.gloss: a shop, a place of business
evidence: M-O s.v. office (place where business is transacted)
terms.comment: The Roman workplace on the street: a banker’s office was a taberna argentāria, a bookseller’s a taberna librāria (Cic. Phil. 2.21, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a study, an office at home
evidence: Vitr. 6.4; Plin. NH 35.7 (Lewis & Short, s.v. tabulīnum)
terms.comment: In a Roman house the room where the family records were kept; in the libellī the room where the father works (see study).

sources: Lewis & Short: officina · Lewis & Short: taberna · Lewis & Short: tablinum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 125, 353, 365.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. office (place where business is transacted, office building, white-collar work-place).
